recipes.name: Easy Chicken à la King
ingredients_raw: 2.25 cups cooked, cubed chicken breast meat

steps.text: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add bell pepper and mushrooms; sauté until tender. Stir in broth and flour; cook, stirring, until thickened. Add chicken; cook until heated through. Remove from heat.
Combine sour cream, egg yolks, sherry, pimento, salt, and black pepper in a small bowl until well mixed; add to chicken mixture. Cook over medium heat until thoroughly heated through, stirring often.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Chicken à la King
raw_recipe.description: This chicken à la king recipe is a skillet dish of cubed chicken, bell pepper, mushrooms, and broth stirred and simmered with a sour cream-sherry sauce.

review.reviewBody: 5 Star Plus - I am switching my allegience from the Chicken a la King I recipe (on this site) to this Chicken a la King III. I've used the other recipe often and loved it as long as you added sherry which was missing from the ingredients. I saw this last night and decided to try it. This is now the one I will make - the ingredients are all on the mark - I just added two minced scallions and a pinch of thyme and cayenne pepper which it didn't need but that I like. Both are 5 star but we prefer this one now.

This is the best chicken a la king recipe that I've fixed and I've tried quite a few over the years. I did it a little different. I used whole chicken breasts and browned them first in my pressure cooker in some vegetable oil. Then I added about 2 cups of water and cooked them in the pressure cooker for about 40 minutes and then took the meat off the bones and proceeded with following the recipe. I had it with some biscuits and corn. Yum!

I made this for dinner tonight and after reading all of the reviews, I did add garlic, onions, celery, carrot and peas which made this extremely awesome. Served over buttermilk biscuits. I also added garlic salt, thyme and lots of pepper while making the sauce. My husband said his mouth is still dancing with flavor. (Mine too). Whoever said this recipe was bland, needs to read the reviews to add more character to the recipe. Loved it!!!!

Great! Regarding 'bland', that opinion has such a wide range. For me this would have been incredibly bland as is, if I didn't do every augmentation reviews suggested. Having never made a la King anything, I used the guts of this recipe and altered:
Fresh mush, onion and carrot sauteed; frozen peas added near the end. 
Added thyme, chili powder, garlic powder, and Worcester. I thought I added ample amounts; could have added even more. I went through a lot of chicken broth, making it more saucy right before serving as we weren't ready to eat right away. I'm shocked my picky spouse liked this, but he did. Go me! I'm normally a terrible cook.

Very good! I did a LOT of variation here. I used a red bell pepper instead of green, and I also added diced snap pea pods. I used canned mushrooms instead of fresh and turkey instead of chicken. I did not add the egg yolks, but a bit more fat free sour cream and broth to keep it creamy. No pimentos either, just didn't have any on hand. I used cornstarch to thicken instead of flour. Instead of serving this over noodles or rice, I made mini phyllo pies. It worked really well! Use 2-3 phyllo sheets, each lightly buttered/oiled. Stack and fold the phyllo so it lines a mini pie tin (oiled) and hangs over the edges. Fill with the a la king and fold the phyllo over the top. Bake at 400 degrees for about 10 minutes. Hubby LOVED it and actually called it "hearty."
Simple and one pan. Can't beat that. Red peppers and peas but otherwise stayed with recipe. Might use base and try ham and carrots or corn another time. Thanks for recipe.

Did make some changes. Used a chopped shallot and minced garlic to saute with mushrooms, 1/2 cup carrots and 1/2 cup frozen peas. I used white wine instead of sherry and added about 1/4 tsp. dried thyme. Turned out great, lots of flavour. Will make again for sure.

The meal was filling. It could use a little more spice from original recipe. I was in a hurry and made this step by step. The reviews are helpful, too bad I read them after I made it. I think next time I will add some peas, carrots and onions. I do like to use up my celery when available which I did. Maybe in the small bowl mix with the eggs, and sour cream some hot sauce could be added. Overall, a filling meal. I suppose chicken a la king can be made to ones liking.

Where are the peas?! Started with a sauté of celery, minced onion and garlic. Added frozen peas during the last few minutes of cooking. Also added a dash of thyme. Used pressure-cooked, shredded chicken. Skipped pimento because I not have it . Served over rice. Will make again!

This was good, but I added a few things. I added minced garlic and thyme when I sauteed the peppers and mushrooms. After I added the chicken the mixture was still bland, so I added garlic salt and onion powder(my husband doesn't like onions so I use powder and he doesn't notice). I didn't have pimentos and it still turned out great.

We thought this was very good, served over rice. In spite of a few minor changes, I pretty much stuck to the recipe. I sauteed onion & garlic since I didn't have any bell pepper or mushrooms, I left out the egg yolks--it was plenty rich anyway--and I added the pimento from a jar. The sherry addition was a perfect touch.
Chicken a la King is my husband's favorite. I used fresh sweet red peppers (not jarred pimentos) and lots of mushrooms. He loved it!
Without peppers I’ll add more pimento next time
This is a very good recipe. It's one of those comforting meals for the cold winter nights. Or anytime. It's excellent server over rice or egg noodles. Thank you for sharing
Not BAD but mind-numbingly bland. Won't make it again.
Loved it, didn’t have peppers.
This was delicious as is.
My whole family loved it! Served with a side of steamed broccoli.

Words cannot describe how delicious this was. Of course I had to double the ingredients to make enough for the family. Although I had to omit the bell pepper and pimento and opted to put in Cream of Chicken, Peas, White Cooking Wine instead. Once I had it cooking I realized that it needed more flavor so I added a House spice blend and Misses Dash Table Blend which finally gave it the flavor of a Chicken Pot Pie. My family enjoyed this and there's no doubt that I will make this again!

This is a very good base, we don't like mushrooms so I used one green, one red pepper and half an onion, It was quite bland when it was done so I added onion salt, garlic powder, seasoning salt and a bit of cayenne pepper. The result was delicious!! Served over biscuits with broccoli - will definitely make again
